message: The Titanic data is a binary classification problem (target Survived). High‑cardinality text columns (Name, Ticket, Cabin) risk overfitting, so we extract useful structure with regexes: Title from Name, CabinDeck from Cabin, and TicketPrefix from Ticket. After extraction we drop the raw high‑cardinality columns. Ticket and Cabin appear in both train and test (test_seen_pct > 0) and rows sharing the same value are likely to have correlated outcomes (family members on the same ticket or cabin), so we add group size counts and group target encoding for these columns (min_group_size=2, smoothing=1.0). Fare is heavily right‑skewed (skew 4.79) so we log‑transform it. Age has missing values; we keep it as is and rely on the model to handle missingness (add_missing_indicators=true). Categorical columns with moderate cardinality (Ticket, Cabin, TicketPrefix, Embarked, Sex) are frequency‑encoded. Text length of Name, Ticket and Cabin may carry signal, so we add length features. No datetime columns exist. The target is binary, so we do not log‑transform it. This plan balances signal extraction with overfitting control.
